core_obligations: Show that elements of N have content ideals, first for elements of the projective spreadout N' and then for general elements by scaling into its image (proof lines 7240-7255).

For u as in (2), reduce to A local, note that each composed map N' -> N -> N -> M is injective modulo the maximal ideal hence universally injective, and pass to the colimit over S (proof lines 7257-7267).
proof_roadmap: Content ideals through the spreadout (proof lines 7240-7255).
Localization and the composed maps (proof lines 7257-7263).
difficulty_reason: In equation labelled equation-star, if a pure spreadout exists then the lemma asserts that elements of N have content ideals in A, and that a morphism u : N -> M to a flat A-module M which is injective modulo every maximal ideal is A-universally injective (statement lines 7228-7238). For the first part the proof chooses U and N' as in the definition of a pure spreadout: every element of N' has a content ideal because N' is A-projective, which follows either directly or from More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-content-exists-flat-Mittag-Leffler together with Algebra, Example labelled algebra-example-ML (proof lines 7240-7250). Since N' -> N is A-universally injective, the image of an element of N' has the same content ideal, and for a general x in N one chooses s in S with s x in the image of N' and uses that x and s x have the same content ideal (proof lines 7252-7255). For the second part the proof reduces to A local at a maximal ideal, and for each s in S considers the composition N' -> N -> N -> M; each map is injective modulo the maximal ideal, so the composition is A-universally injective by Lemma labelled lemma-universally-injective-local, and since N is the colimit of the (1/s)N' one concludes that u is a colimit of universally injective maps and hence universally injective (proof lines 7257-7267; the localization reduction is marked 'small detail omitted'). Reducing universal injectivity of u to the projective spreadout and then passing to the colimit over S is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
